FROMGIT: ASoC: AMD: Always stop ch2 first Commit 6b116dfb4633a ("ASoC: AMD: make channel 1 dma as circular") made both channels circular, so this comment and logic no longer applies. Always stop ch2 (the channel closest to the output) before ch1. This ensures that the downstream circular DMA channel does not continue to play/capture repeated samples after the upstream circular DMA channel has already stopped. Signed-off-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org> (cherry picked from commit 30896d3619bd80486a3f8a75d62ea3b58fc61ad5 https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/broonie/sound.git) BUG=b:111073426 TEST=(with all patches in series) capture & playback to headphones # cat /proc/interrupts | grep ACP_IRQ # arecord -D hw:0,1 -f dat -d 1 /tmp/t1.wav # cat /proc/interrupts | grep ACP_IRQ Difference between ACP_IRQ interrupt count is ~= 46 TEST=(with all patches in series) capture from DMIC & playback to speakers # aplay -D hw:0,0 -f dat /tmp/t1.wav # arecord -D hw:0,3 -f dat -d 1 /tmp/t1.wav # cat /proc/interrupts | grep ACP_IRQ aplay -D hw:0,2 -f dat /tmp/t1.wav Change-Id: Icfa19cfee31594268bcb374332d8f6cfbd34cf9e Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1123301 Commit-Ready: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Tested-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org>

FROMGIT: ASoC: AMD: Always subtract bytescount It is always correct to subtract out the starting bytescount value. Even in the case of 2^64 byte rollover (292 Million Years in the future @ 48000 Hz) the math still works out. Signed-off-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org> (cherry picked from commit 715cdce04487fb23d5c10693b3bc01309fea955a https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/broonie/sound.git) BUG=b:111073426 TEST=(with all patches in series) capture & playback to headphones # cat /proc/interrupts | grep ACP_IRQ # arecord -D hw:0,1 -f dat -d 1 /tmp/t1.wav # cat /proc/interrupts | grep ACP_IRQ => Difference between ACP_IRQ interrupt count is ~= 46 # aplay -D hw:0,0 -f dat /tmp/t1.wav => Sound plays out of Headphones TEST=(with all patches in series) capture from DMIC & playback to speakers # cat /proc/interrupts | grep ACP_IRQ # arecord -D hw:0,3 -f dat -d 1 /tmp/t1.wav # cat /proc/interrupts | grep ACP_IRQ => Difference between ACP_IRQ interrupt count is ~= 46 # aplay -D hw:0,2 -f dat /tmp/t1.wav => Sound plays out of speakers Change-Id: Ifd472275ea0f5ea33a2a72661987873e7a102a9a Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1123303 Commit-Ready: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Tested-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org>

FROMGIT: ASoC: AMD: Fix Capture DMA channel names On capture, audio data is first copied from I2S to ACP memory, and then to SYSRAM. For each step the channel number increases, so the names in the driver were wrong. Signed-off-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org> (cherry picked from commit 55af49ac1b8627dfbfa2689af118d994d7a0ba1b https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/broonie/sound.git) BUG=b:111073426 TEST=(with all patches in series) capture & playback to headphones # cat /proc/interrupts | grep ACP_IRQ # arecord -D hw:0,1 -f dat -d 1 /tmp/t1.wav # cat /proc/interrupts | grep ACP_IRQ => Difference between ACP_IRQ interrupt count is ~= 46 # aplay -D hw:0,0 -f dat /tmp/t1.wav => Sound plays out of Headphones TEST=(with all patches in series) capture from DMIC & playback to speakers # cat /proc/interrupts | grep ACP_IRQ # arecord -D hw:0,3 -f dat -d 1 /tmp/t1.wav # cat /proc/interrupts | grep ACP_IRQ => Difference between ACP_IRQ interrupt count is ~= 46 # aplay -D hw:0,2 -f dat /tmp/t1.wav => Sound plays out of speakers Change-Id: I9d13f049d796c61c09da9935dc58d747486426bd Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1123304 Commit-Ready: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Tested-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org>

FROMGIT: ASoC: AMD: Do not generate interrups for every captured sample On capture, audio data is first copied from I2S to ACP memory, and then from ACP to SYSRAM. The I2S_TO_ACP_DMA interrupt fires on every sample transferred from I2S to ACP memory. That is it fires ~48000 times per second when capturing @ 48 kHz. Since we don't do anything on this interrupt anyway, disable it to save quite a few unnecessary interrupts. The real "work" (calling snd_pcm_period_elapsed()) is done when transfer from ACP to SYSRAM is complete. Signed-off-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org> (cherry picked from commit 8c6b964eddd2c39a9796899b2be099ece1b6c6ca https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/broonie/sound.git) BUG=b:111073426 TEST=(with all patches in series) capture & playback to headphones # cat /proc/interrupts | grep ACP_IRQ # arecord -D hw:0,1 -f dat -d 1 /tmp/t1.wav # cat /proc/interrupts | grep ACP_IRQ => Difference between ACP_IRQ interrupt count is ~= 46 # aplay -D hw:0,0 -f dat /tmp/t1.wav => Sound plays out of Headphones TEST=(with all patches in series) capture from DMIC & playback to speakers # cat /proc/interrupts | grep ACP_IRQ # arecord -D hw:0,3 -f dat -d 1 /tmp/t1.wav # cat /proc/interrupts | grep ACP_IRQ => Difference between ACP_IRQ interrupt count is ~= 46 # aplay -D hw:0,2 -f dat /tmp/t1.wav => Sound plays out of speakers Change-Id: I945c2637965858bac2ae53ed44f1d4a6d3600e88 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1123305 Commit-Ready: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Tested-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org>

FROMGIT: ASoC: AMD: Reset bytescount when starting transaction The pointer() callback gets its value by reading the I2S BYTE_COUNT register. This is a 64-bit runnning transaction counter. If a transaction was aborted in the middle of a sample buffer, the counter will stop counting on a number divisible by the buffer size. Since we actually use it as a pointer into an aligned buffer, however, we do want to ensure that it always starts at a number divisible by the buffer size when starting a transaction, hence we reset it whenever starting a transaction. To accomplish this, it wasn't necessary to zero bytescount at the termination of each transaction, so remove this unnecessary code. Signed-off-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org> (cherry picked from commit 1a337a1e7885085d224583c766614e5945bde671 https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/broonie/sound.git) BUG=b:111073426 TEST=(with all patches in series) capture & playback to headphones # cat /proc/interrupts | grep ACP_IRQ # arecord -D hw:0,1 -f dat -d 1 /tmp/t1.wav # cat /proc/interrupts | grep ACP_IRQ => Difference between ACP_IRQ interrupt count is ~= 46 # aplay -D hw:0,0 -f dat /tmp/t1.wav => Sound plays out of Headphones TEST=(with all patches in series) capture from DMIC & playback to speakers # cat /proc/interrupts | grep ACP_IRQ # arecord -D hw:0,3 -f dat -d 1 /tmp/t1.wav # cat /proc/interrupts | grep ACP_IRQ => Difference between ACP_IRQ interrupt count is ~= 46 # aplay -D hw:0,2 -f dat /tmp/t1.wav => Sound plays out of speakers Change-Id: I0b1a657417fc8104930ae5ded338fabbe165c245 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1123302 Commit-Ready: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Tested-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org>

FROMGIT: ASoC: AMD: Simplify trigger handler Now that the I2S channel names are fixed, and DMA data flow order is consistent (ch1 then ch2), we can simplify channel start order: start the upstream channel and then the downstream channel for both playback and capture cases. Signed-off-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org> (cherry picked from commit df61f9f76609456efbc60d495b3235baf7d07691 https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/broonie/sound.git) BUG=b:111073426 TEST=(with all patches in series) capture & playback to headphones # cat /proc/interrupts | grep ACP_IRQ # arecord -D hw:0,1 -f dat -d 1 /tmp/t1.wav # cat /proc/interrupts | grep ACP_IRQ => Difference between ACP_IRQ interrupt count is ~= 46 # aplay -D hw:0,0 -f dat /tmp/t1.wav => Sound plays out of Headphones TEST=(with all patches in series) capture from DMIC & playback to speakers # cat /proc/interrupts | grep ACP_IRQ # arecord -D hw:0,3 -f dat -d 1 /tmp/t1.wav # cat /proc/interrupts | grep ACP_IRQ => Difference between ACP_IRQ interrupt count is ~= 46 # aplay -D hw:0,2 -f dat /tmp/t1.wav => Sound plays out of speakers Change-Id: I9deb98dbd6b6451d70ff839351811eca095c70c2 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1123306 Commit-Ready: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Tested-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org>

BACKPORT: CHROMIUM: esdfs: Don't cache unused entries If someone changes a file behind esdfs's back, either by modifying the lower fs, or by accesssing it through a separate mount, we fail to notice until esdfs attempts to access it. This can cause issues when deleting a file, as esdfs holds a reference and prevents the file from being fully deleted. Instead, don't maintain unused entries in the cache. Since it's all in memory, this should have minimal performance impact, but will greatly improve consistency with the lower filesystem. BUG=b:63876697 BUG=b:110204200 TEST=Create file through esdfs, delete on lower, check that space is freed.
